messages:
support-sophie: Hey folks, multiple customers in AP-SOUTH reporting spikes and 502s starting ~08:12 UTC. Tickets say traffic routed to US-WEST for some requests.
ops-bot: [alert] route-change detected: service=redwood-inference-api env=prod from=ap-south to=us-west at 08:11:56 UTC :rotating_light:
maya: @support-sophie can you paste the ticket IDs? curious if it's all tenants or just a subset.
support-sophie: TKT-32451, TKT-32458. Both on dedicated capacity but same region tag ap-south. Users saw latency jump from ~60ms -> 750ms and occasional 502s.
lucas: pulling probe logs now. short dump:
```
2026-03-16T08:11:45Z probe[ap-south-1]: health=OK latency=55ms
2026-03-16T08:11:50Z probe[ap-south-1]: health=DEGRADED status=502
2026-03-16T08:11:51Z control-plane: mark instance unhealthy -> route to fallback us-west
2026-03-16T08:11:52Z probe[ap-south-1]: health=OK latency=60ms
```
maya: looks like a transient 502 triggered failover despite quick recovery. whats our healthcheck policy? sam: current config uses 2 consecutive failures within 10s to mark unhealthy, and a 1-check recovery window. That explains immediate failover then quick flapping.
tara: I recall a recent deploy changed probe type from TCP to HTTP and introduced a short timeout 200ms -> 100ms. Could be more sensitive to GC pauses on instances. @sam can you confirm recent config diff?
sam: confirmed. diff in commitments repo:
```
probes:
  interval: 5s
  timeout: 100ms   # was 200ms
  failures: 2
  recoveries: 1
```
maya: so shorter timeout + transient backend 502s = false positive. Also noticed routing decision used stale region metadata on control-plane; lucas any evidence?
lucas: yes. control-plane log:
```
2026-03-16T08:11:51Z control-plane: selected fallback region=us-west for tenant=acme-inc reason=UNHEALTHY(ap-south-1) cached_region_tag=ap-south-1 last_sync=2026-03-15T03:00:12Z
```
lucas: last_sync for region tags was >24h ago for that control-plane shard due to a stuck sync job.
tara: oh — so two independent issues: (1) probe timeout too aggressive causing false negative -> failover, (2) region-tag sync lag causing fallback to pick a nonoptimal region mapping if re-eval needed.
support-sophie: customers report higher cost due to cross-region egress, and SLO breaches. They want rollback or mitigation ASAP.
maya: mitigation plan:
- increase probe timeout back to 200ms (sam)
- bump recoveries to 2 to avoid single-check flip (sam)
- restart control-plane sync job and force re-sync of region tags (lucas)
- temporarily relax automatic failover to prefer local region if within X ms of healthy (tara)
sam: applying probe changes to staging now, will patch prod config if tests good. deploying in ~7m.
lucas: restarting sync job on shard-3 now `systemctl restart region-sync@3` — monitoring.
ops-bot: [event] config-update scheduled by sam at 08:18:40 UTC
maya: repro steps for oncall docs (for triage):
1) use curl against synthetic health endpoint from ap-south:
   `curl -v -H "Host: inference.prod" https://ap-south.health/redwood/probe`
2) inject transient 502 from backend (simulate fast GC or routing hiccup)
3) observe probe timeout behavior and control-plane decision in `/var/log/control-plane.log`

lucas: control-plane sync finished at 08:19:02 UTC, region tags updated.
sam: prod probe config rolled at 08:25:10 UTC, increased timeout -> 200ms and recoveries=2. No further automatic failovers observed since.
support-sophie: notified impacted customers with explanation + credit offer. They're checking if their traffic returned to ap-south.
maya: follow-ups: add metric for probe-flap-rate per-region, add alert when region-tag sync > 5m, and add cooldown window to failover policy to avoid single-check flips. assigning jira INF-872 to me.
tara: also putting a test in CI that verifies probe timeout change doesn't regress latency on our microbench harness.
maya: thanks team :thumbsup: closing this thread once INF-872 is up and customers ack recovery.
